entries.description: Epoch AI's back-of-envelope estimate of energy used by a typical GPT-4o query, including server and datacenter overhead.
entries.source_title: How much energy does ChatGPT use?
entries.evidence: queries using GPT-4o likely consume roughly 0.3 watt-hours
entries.notes: Scope: NOT GPU-only. The estimate assumes ≈1 s of H100 time × 1500 W × 70% utilization, and the 1500 W per H100 includes server and datacenter overhead (the source puts datacenter-level overhead at 10-20%). Per-query (not per-token), inference only. Longer inputs use more: the same article gives about 2.5 Wh for ~10k input tokens and ~40 Wh for ~100k, so 0.3 Wh is a typical figure, not a ceiling. Verified 2026-09-29 by maintainer via manual fetch of the primary source (this environment cannot reach it).

entries.description: Price ratio per decision, Jev / comparison LLM, from TypeSafe's own workflow-eval cost table (all LLM configurations in it).
entries.derivation: geometric_mean over every workflow-eval LLM configuration of typesafe_cost_per_case_usd / typesafe_eval_<config>_cost_usd; range = [min, max] of those ratios
entries.notes: This is the model's 'q' parameter default. Jev's $0.0004 is rounded (±12.5%), so every ratio shares that uncertainty; the range here is the spread across configurations only (the rounding is covered in r_energy_ratio's range, the one the Monte Carlo samples). Sensitivity: restricting to configurations within about 1 accuracy point of Jev gives q_price_ratio_accuracy_matched. See METHODOLOGY.md §5(a).

entries.description: Sensitivity check for q: the same price ratio restricted to the workflow-eval configurations whose accuracy is within about 1 point of Jev's.
entries.derivation: geometric_mean of typesafe_cost_per_case_usd / typesafe_eval_<config>_cost_usd for config in (sonnet_5, terra, luna)
entries.notes: Not a model input; shown to make the sensitivity of q to the choice of comparison LLMs visible. See METHODOLOGY.md §5(a).

entries.description: Cost-proxy estimator for the energy ratio per decision, under the explicit assumption that energy is proportional to price.
entries.derivation: = q_price_ratio (cost-proportionality assumption, stated explicitly, see METHODOLOGY.md §5(a))
entries.notes: One of the three proxies combined into r_energy_ratio. TypeSafe states it cannot prove its price is not subsidized, so this proxy may UNDERSTATE r (make Jev look more energy-efficient than it is). See METHODOLOGY.md §5(a).

entries.description: Latency-proxy estimator for the energy ratio per decision, under the explicit assumption that energy scales with compute time on comparable hardware/batching.
entries.derivation: geometric_mean over every workflow-eval LLM configuration of typesafe_latency_per_case_s / typesafe_eval_<config>_latency_s; range = [min, max] of those ratios
entries.notes: One of the three proxies combined into r_energy_ratio. Uses the same eval and measurement setup for Jev and every LLM configuration (like-for-like), instead of the generic 70-500 ms headline range. TypeSafe ran the evals from its own laptops on the US West Coast, so the latencies include network time. See METHODOLOGY.md §5(b).

entries.description: Token-count-proxy estimator for the energy ratio per decision, under the explicit assumption that energy scales linearly with output token count.
entries.notes: One of the three proxies (the only one from a source independent of TypeSafe) combined into r_energy_ratio. See METHODOLOGY.md §5(c) for the stated linear-scaling assumption and its likely bias direction (ignores input-side compute and architecture differences).

entries.description: The model's default energy-ratio-per-decision parameter (r), combining the three proxies (cost, latency, tokens).
entries.derivation: geometric_mean(r_cost_proxy, r_latency_proxy, r_tokens_proxy) as the point estimate; range = [min, max] of (r_cost_proxy.range, r_latency_proxy.range, r_tokens_proxy.value), widened on both sides to cover the rounding of Jev's published cost and latency (see notes and METHODOLOGY.md §5)
entries.notes: This is the model's 'r' parameter default and the range the Monte Carlo samples. No public Wh/joules figure for Jev exists, so this three-proxy envelope is the best available substitute for a measurement. Widening: Jev's $0.0004 and 0.4 s are rounded, so their true values lie within ±12.5%; the lower bound is multiplied by 0.875 and the upper bound by 1.125, which covers every cost or latency ratio Jev's unrounded values could produce. See METHODOLOGY.md §5.

entries.description: The model's default baseline annual AI inference energy (E0) in the AI-focused-datacenter, 2025 scope -- the total pool from which the decision-task share s is drawn, not itself decision-specific.
entries.derivation: iea_ai_focused_dc_2025_twh * inference_share_of_ai_compute; range = [iea_ai_focused_dc_2025_twh.range.min * inference_share_of_ai_compute.range.min, iea_ai_focused_dc_2025_twh.range.max * inference_share_of_ai_compute.range.max]
entries.notes: Compounds two independently wide uncertainties (see iea_ai_focused_dc_2025_twh and inference_share_of_ai_compute). This is the whole-inference baseline; 's' (the decision-task share of this) is applied on top, separately, inside model.js.

entries.description: Assumed own-price elasticity of demand for decision-task volume with respect to the cost of a decision (JEV plus any residual LLM call).
entries.source_title: The Rebound Effect: An Assessment of the Evidence for Economy-wide Energy Savings from Improved Energy Efficiency
entries.publisher: UK Energy Research Centre (UKERC) / Steven Sorrell, 2007
entries.evidence: direct rebound effects typically 10-30%; economy-wide estimates 37% to over 100% in some studies
entries.notes: The literature gives REBOUND PERCENTAGES for other sectors, not a price elasticity of demand for AI decision-inference calls (no such study exists). The specific numeric range chosen here straddles this model's own eps=1 backfire threshold as a deliberate judgment call, explicitly NOT a citation-backed number for AI decisions specifically — see METHODOLOGY.md §6. Bibliographic details (Steven Sorrell, UKERC, 1 October 2007) verified 2026-09-29 by maintainer via manual fetch of the primary source (this environment cannot reach it). The percentages quoted in 'evidence' are in the full report and were NOT re-verified, so this entry stays 'unverified' for its numeric evidence.
